critiques.description: The mapping for req-AI-003 concludes that the requirement is only "partially_satisfied," but the attached evidence does not establish the requirement text or its success criteria, so the degree of satisfaction is not supported by the cited material.
critiques.rationale: Map-027 states that req-AI-003 applies because customer invoice content is sent from the Invoice Agent to a hosted model provider and that the requirement is only partially satisfied because the documentation describes "only parsed invoice details" being returned to the model but does not explain why that scope is necessary. The evidence cited for this mapping (evd-001, evd-004, evd-005) supports the data flow and the shape of the invoice object: evd-001 documents that the agent is backed by a hosted model provider; evd-004 documents that `process_invoice` returns a validated invoice object with amount, submitter, category, and due date; evd-005 documents that the invoice file’s contents are parsed and returned to the model as invoice details. None of these passages provide the text of req-AI-003, describe its exact documentation requirements, or discuss any design rationale justifying why these particular fields (and only these fields) must be sent. As eas-048 already notes, the "what is sent" aspect is documented, but the classification of req-AI-003 as "partially_satisfied" versus "unverified" rests on requirement details and rationale that are not established by the cited evidence. Under the evidence policy, this makes the partial-satisfaction conclusion unsupported: the available material demonstrates applicability and documents the data shared, but does not justify a specific satisfaction level. This situation is better treated as a documentation gap about req-AI-003’s satisfaction status until requirement text and rationale are provided.
